title: Dad of 20-year-old co-pilot in Florida Learjet crash says final radio calls showed 'she's tough'
summary: The father of the 20-year-old co-pilot who died along with eight others when their Learjet crashed in Florida said Friday he has listened to his daughter's heartbreaking final radio transmissions…

image.caption: Allan Filgueiras, whose daughter Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras was the co-pilot of a Learjet that crashed and killed nine people, attends a news conference in Coral Gables, Fla., on Friday. (WSVN/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: The father of the 20-year-old co-pilot who died along with eight others when their Learjet crashed in Florida said Friday he has listened to his daughter's heartbreaking final radio transmissions "many times" since the crash.
Family held news conference to push back against online criticism over her age, experience

Allan Filgueiras, himself a pilot, was searching for answers as to why the plane plunged from the sky on Sunday — but what he found was immense pride in how his daughter, Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, handled the crisis.
"I did listen to that many times trying to find a clue. In my head. How'd that happen? And wow, she's tough," Allan Filgueiras said at a news conference Friday, frequently holding back tears.

In her final conversation with air traffic control, she can be heard calmly reporting ice buildup on the plane as the Learjet flew into a thunderstorm and turbulence tossed it up and down by 200 metres. The situation quickly escalated as the aircraft fell at breathtaking speed. "Declare an emergency 722-Bravo-Delta. We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute!" she said.
Her father and aviation safety experts have been impressed that Filgueiras continued to call out updates on what was happening even as she realized the plane's fate was sealed.
"For the family — it's like having the heart torn from my chest," her father said in Spanish. "I have to find a way to go on living."
Florida crash: How did this private jet fall out of the sky? | About That

The family wants to push back against online criticism over whether she had enough experience to be in the cockpit of a Learjet. She had more than 1,300 hours of experience and completed extensive training to earn her commercial pilot's licence.
So her father held Friday's news conference, which his lawyer said was designed to "preserve not just her memory, but her reputation."

"She was at the top of her class in everything that she did, and she was perfectly qualified to be the co-pilot on this flight, despite her tender years," attorney Stuart Grossman said, noting there were no immediate plans to file a lawsuit over the crash.

It's far too early in the National Transportation Safety Board's investigation to know what caused the crash. As it fell, the Learjet accelerated beyond its design limits and pieces of the plane's tail were found kilometres away from the crash site.

Retired airline pilot John Cox, who is now the CEO of Safety Operating Systems, said he started out flying professionally at age 19, meaning he was in the same situation as Filgueiras when he started his career. He said she was doing quite well to earn the co-pilot's seat she had.
"To be in the right seat of a Lear 60, she had to impress somebody, because that's a good ride. I mean, that's great. I know she loved it," Cox said.
Her father believes she held up in the midst of a crisis better than most.

"She showed me what it is to be a hero because once you see that coming, a lot of the big boys — military or whatever — they can't handle. And she was the one over there to the last minute fighting," Allan Filgueiras said.

The victims included technology entrepreneur Adam Robinson; his wife, Helen Sharp; and their two young children, relatives said. The family's nanny, Ana María Ramírez Cetina, was also killed. The plane's captain, who was pilot in command as the plane fell, was 55-year-old Jeff Gregory.
